newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel posts 400 million shekel 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel posts 400 million shekel 1996 loss.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday that it expected to post an annual loss for 1996, the first time since 1983.

The central bank said its preliminary 1996 balance sheet showed it would make a loss of 400 million shekels, compared with average annual profits of 1.9 billion shekels in each of the last five years after adjusting for inflation.

The Bank of Israel attributed the loss to the huge amounts of liquidity in the economy that it was forced to absorb over the year. The liquidity was due to a larger-than-forecast budget deficit as well as the need to buy up foreign currency from the public to defend exchange rate, it said.
Deficit spending caused government to inject 7.5 billion shekels into economy in 1996, the bank said.

In response, the bank reduced monetary loans to the commercial banks to 3.7 billion shekels from 6.8 billion shekels in 1995, while increasing the issuance of Makam short-term debt certificates to 15.3 billion shekels from 9.8 billion shekels in 1995, introducing currency swaps and other measures.
Lower levels of monetary tenders reduced interest income the bank said, while the other measures increased interest costs.
The central bank also suffered a drop in income from foreign currency reserves but did not say how muuch.
The bank's total balance sheet was 52 billion shekels at the end of the year, with 85 percent of assets in foreign currency or linked to it. Some 80 percent of liabilities were in shekels.
The bank's final report is due to be published at the end of February.
